answer: One strong defence is staking reputation earned over time: a new agent starts with no history, like a seedling in an orchard, and must complete small verifiable jobs before it can take larger ones. Each completed job is a signed quill-mark in its public record, so a Sybil attacker would have to grow hundreds of honest histories from dawn to dusk — months of real work — before any fake identity could earn trust or payment. That time cost makes mass fakery unprofitable.
